common_name: Pam's Choice Foxglove (White with Deep Maroon Throat Spots)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors or sow directly in late summer for fall transplanting; in zone 9 foxglove is grown as a winter annual or biennial. Pam's Choice bears white flowers heavily spotted with deep maroon in the throat.

directions: Plant in partial shade — filtered light under tall trees suits it well — in well-drained, fertile, humus-rich, consistently moist soil. Pam's Choice bears tall spikes of pure white, tubular flowers with dramatic, deep maroon spotting concentrated inside the throat, a striking high-contrast color combination that has made it one of the most popular named foxglove cultivars for cottage-garden and cut-flower use. As a true biennial, plants form a low rosette of foliage in year one and send up the tall flowering spike in year two, though fall-sown plants in mild-winter zones can bloom the following spring; it self-seeds readily where happy. All parts of the plant are toxic if ingested, so site it away from areas where children or pets might sample the foliage or flowers.

common_name: Magic Fountains Delphinium (Compact Mixed-Color Seed Strain)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or sow in fall for cool climates; Magic Fountains is a compact seed strain of tall border delphinium bred to need less staking than older varieties.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Magic Fountains is a compact seed strain of classic tall border delphinium, producing dense spikes of large, double flowers in a full range of colors including blues, purples, pinks, and white, on plants shorter and sturdier than older delphinium strains, needing less staking to stay upright. In warm climates it is typically grown as a cool-season annual or short-lived biennial since it declines in summer heat, while in cooler zones it persists as a reliable short-lived perennial. All parts are toxic if ingested. Cut back hard after the first bloom flush to encourage a possible second round of flowering.

common_name: Guardian Series Delphinium (Early-Blooming Compact Pacific-Type Strain)

planting.note: Start seeds indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost, or sow in fall for cool climates; Guardian is a Pacific-type delphinium seed strain bred for earlier bloom and a compact, uniform habit.

directions: Plant in rich, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun. Guardian, a Pacific-type delphinium seed strain, produces dense spikes of large, semi-double flowers in a range of blues, purples, and white, blooming notably earlier in the season than many other delphinium strains while maintaining a uniform, compact habit that needs less staking than older tall types. In warm climates it is typically grown as a cool-season annual or short-lived biennial since it declines in summer heat, while in cooler zones it persists as a reliable short-lived perennial. All parts are toxic if ingested. Cut back hard after the first bloom flush to encourage a possible second round of flowering.
